preconditions.expression: n >= 2 and m >= 1 and all(1 <= v <= n and 1 <= u <= n and v != u for v, u in roads)
preconditions.description: The input consists of n cities (2 ≤ n ≤ 100) and m bidirectional roads (m ≥ 1), where each road connects two distinct cities (1 ≤ v, u ≤ n).

preconditions.expression: len(roads) == m and all(roads.count((v, u)) == 1 and roads.count((u, v)) == 1 for v, u in roads)
preconditions.description: Each pair of cities is connected by at most one road (undirected, no duplicates).
The road network is connected (any city can be reached from any other city via roads).

postconditions.description: The output is the maximum possible average number of safe roads among all shortest paths from city 1 (culture capital) to city n (main capital), where a road is safe if it has the police station at one of its endpoints. The answer is printed as a float with absolute or relative inaccuracy ≤ 10^-6.

postconditions.expression: all(0 <= float(stdout) <= m for _ in range(1))
postconditions.description: The output value is a non-negative float representing the average safe roads, bounded by the total number of roads m.
